The test image shows a very young soybean seedling barely emerging from wet, dark soil. The hypocotyl appears brownish/discolored and the seedling looks weak/struggling. This is a seedling-stage disease affecting the root/hypocotyl area.

Top candidates from the part index (root/whole_plant/seed categories for seedling diseases):
- **Pythium_damping_off** - water-soaked lesions, brown soft rot
- **Rhizoctonia** - reddish-brown, sunken, dry lesions on hypocotyl
- **Phytophthora** - brown root rot
- **Fusarium** - poor emergence, reddish-brown roots

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with one from each candidate.
Pythium reference shows a rotting seedling in wet soil - similar context but the cotyledons look more rotted/brown. Let me check Rhizoctonia.
Rhizoctonia shows older seedlings with distinct sunken lesions at the soil line - different stage than the test image. Let me check Fusarium.
Fusarium reference shows a mature stem/root - not matching the seedling stage. Let me check Phytophthora.
Phytophthora shows field-level wilting, not matching. Pythium was closest so far. Let me check more references to confirm. Let me look at Pythium seed reference and Rhizoctonia root.
Very similar! Pythium seed reference shows a young seedling in wet soil with discolored tissue - closely matches the test image. Let me check Rhizoctonia root for comparison.
Rhizoctonia root shows mature roots with distinct lesions - not matching. Let me use remaining views on Pythium seed and Phytophthora stem for completeness.
Another strong match - rotting seedling in wet soil. Let me use my last view to check one more class.

SCN root shows mature root system with cysts - completely different from the test image.

**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows:
- Very young soybean seedling barely emerging from soil
- Wet, dark soil conditions
- Brownish/discolored hypocotyl
- Cotyledons just emerging, appearing somewhat water-soaked
- Plant residue on soil surface

The Pythium damping-off references (all 3 viewed) were the strongest visual matches:
- Same seedling stage
- Same wet soil conditions
- Same brown, water-soaked appearance of emerging seedlings
- Matches the symptom description: "water-soaked lesions on hypocotyl or cotyledons developing into brown soft rot; rotted roots"

Other candidates were ruled out: Rhizoctonia shows firm, dry, sunken lesions on older seedlings; Fusarium shows mature plant root rot; Phytophthora shows field-level wilting or stem discoloration; SCN shows root cysts.
